headline: Explicit Models Recover Hidden Rates and Zero-Inflation in Genomic Data
label: Explicit Latent Structure Inference
summary: Simulation-based and EM-based estimators now infer local recombination, mutation, and sampling-zero processes directly rather than absorbing them as noise.
synthesis: The common thread across these items is replacing a simplifying assumption with an explicit model of an unobserved process. Neural posterior estimation, applied via simulation, infers gene-specific recombination and mutation rates in bacterial genomes, with attention to local hotspots. TestNet-PA addresses sampling zeros in microbial presence-absence data through an EM-based quasi-likelihood, aiming for better FDR control in co-occurrence network inference. TCRi, a hierarchical Bayesian information-theoretic framework with a VAE embedding, infers clonotype-phenotype joint distributions from paired scRNA and TCR sequencing, applying the same latent-structure logic to T cell dynamics. What is new is the target: local, gene-level rates and zero-inflation are estimated directly rather than absorbed into noise. The shared element is latent structure made explicit, though the three items operate on different data modalities and inference machinery.
